cases.architecture: MCP server on @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.17 (McpServer with registerTool/registerResource/registerPrompt) exposed both over StdioServerTransport and over a StreamableHTTPServerTransport mounted on Express 4, with every read and write going through the @aws-sdk/lib-dynamodb DynamoDBDocumentClient, and the caller's identity coming from a bearer token resolved into a DynamoDB session row over HTTP and from the invoking local process over stdio.
cases.why: support_ticket_get reads whatever ticket the model names in `ticketId` with a GetCommand keyed on that reference alone and hands the row back, internal notes included. The HTTP session that carries the caller's accountId is available in `ctx` but is only used for the audit line, so any bearer session - or any reference the model picked up from attacker-written ticket text - returns another account's ticket.

cases.architecture: MCP server on @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.17 (McpServer with registerTool/registerResource/registerPrompt) exposed both over StdioServerTransport and over a StreamableHTTPServerTransport mounted on Express 4, with every read and write going through the @aws-sdk/lib-dynamodb DynamoDBDocumentClient, and the caller's identity coming from a bearer token resolved into a DynamoDB session row over HTTP and from the invoking local process over stdio.
cases.why: Same GetCommand against the same tickets table, but the ticket is only rendered when `ticket.accountId === scope`, where `scope` comes from `accountScope(ctx, accountId)` - the session wins and the tool argument is only consulted when there is no session, i.e. over stdio - and the timeline Query carries that same scope in its KeyConditionExpression.

cases.architecture: MCP server on @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.17 (McpServer with registerTool/registerResource/registerPrompt) exposed both over StdioServerTransport and over a StreamableHTTPServerTransport mounted on Express 4, with every read and write going through the @aws-sdk/lib-dynamodb DynamoDBDocumentClient, and the caller's identity coming from a bearer token resolved into a DynamoDB session row over HTTP and from the invoking local process over stdio.
cases.why: The `field` argument is interpolated into the ScanCommand's FilterExpression. A model-chosen value such as `attribute_not_exists(zzz) OR ticketId` expands to `attribute_not_exists(zzz) OR ticketId = :value AND accountId = :accountId`, and because AND binds tighter than OR the account clause stops constraining anything, so the full-table Scan returns every tenant's tickets. Binding the value as a parameter does nothing for the injected attribute name.

cases.architecture: MCP server on @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.17 (McpServer with registerTool/registerResource/registerPrompt) exposed both over StdioServerTransport and over a StreamableHTTPServerTransport mounted on Express 4, with every read and write going through the @aws-sdk/lib-dynamodb DynamoDBDocumentClient, and the caller's identity coming from a bearer token resolved into a DynamoDB session row over HTTP and from the invoking local process over stdio.
cases.why: The caller still chooses which attribute to match on, but `field` is a zod enum mapped through FILTERABLE_ATTRIBUTES and passed as an ExpressionAttributeNames placeholder, so the FilterExpression is a constant string and the `accountId = :accountId` clause cannot be detached or widened.

cases.architecture: MCP server on @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.17 (McpServer with registerTool/registerResource/registerPrompt) exposed both over StdioServerTransport and over a StreamableHTTPServerTransport mounted on Express 4, with every read and write going through the @aws-sdk/lib-dynamodb DynamoDBDocumentClient, and the caller's identity coming from a bearer token resolved into a DynamoDB session row over HTTP and from the invoking local process over stdio.
cases.why: account_credit_apply moves money - an UpdateCommand that increments creditBalanceMinor by up to 5000.00 per call - and never looks at `ctx.session.role`; `requireRole` is imported nowhere in this module. The comment relies on the HTTP transport handing out a role-filtered tool list, but tools/call is not gated by tools/list, so a `support_agent` session (or any session at all) can credit the account it is bound to.

cases.architecture: MCP server on @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.17 (McpServer with registerTool/registerResource/registerPrompt) exposed both over StdioServerTransport and over a StreamableHTTPServerTransport mounted on Express 4, with every read and write going through the @aws-sdk/lib-dynamodb DynamoDBDocumentClient, and the caller's identity coming from a bearer token resolved into a DynamoDB session row over HTTP and from the invoking local process over stdio.
cases.why: The same shape - an UpdateCommand on the accounts table driven straight from tool arguments - but `requireRole(ctx, 'billing_admin')` runs before anything is written and the handler returns `isError: true` for every other session role. The permissive branch inside requireRole only fires when there is no session, which is only the stdio transport, where the process already runs with the operator's own credentials.

cases.architecture: MCP server on @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.17 (McpServer with registerTool/registerResource/registerPrompt) exposed both over StdioServerTransport and over a StreamableHTTPServerTransport mounted on Express 4, with every read and write going through the @aws-sdk/lib-dynamodb DynamoDBDocumentClient, and the caller's identity coming from a bearer token resolved into a DynamoDB session row over HTTP and from the invoking local process over stdio.
cases.why: `sourceUrl` is chosen by the model from text it was shown - a ticket body an attacker can write - and is handed to fetch with no scheme, host or address check, and the response body is both stored and returned as tool content. http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/ or any internal admin endpoint is fetched and read back by the caller. `z.string().url()` constrains the shape of the argument, not its destination.

cases.architecture: MCP server on @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.17 (McpServer with registerTool/registerResource/registerPrompt) exposed both over StdioServerTransport and over a StreamableHTTPServerTransport mounted on Express 4, with every read and write going through the @aws-sdk/lib-dynamodb DynamoDBDocumentClient, and the caller's identity coming from a bearer token resolved into a DynamoDB session row over HTTP and from the invoking local process over stdio.
cases.why: Also fetches a caller-supplied URL and returns the body, but only after parsing it with `new URL()`, requiring `https:`, and requiring exact-hostname membership in the configured `allowedStatusHosts` set - and the request runs with `redirect: 'error'`, so an allowed vendor host cannot bounce it onto an internal address.

cases.architecture: MCP server on @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.17 (McpServer with registerTool/registerResource/registerPrompt) exposed both over StdioServerTransport and over a StreamableHTTPServerTransport mounted on Express 4, with every read and write going through the @aws-sdk/lib-dynamodb DynamoDBDocumentClient, and the caller's identity coming from a bearer token resolved into a DynamoDB session row over HTTP and from the invoking local process over stdio.
cases.why: The `{path}` variable of `runbook://runbooks/{path}` is percent-decoded when the SDK matches the URI and is then joined onto storagePaths.runbookRoot with no normalisation and no containment check, so a client-constructed URI such as runbook://runbooks/..%2f..%2f..%2fetc%2fpasswd makes readFile return any file the process can read as resource contents. The comment's claim that a template variable cannot cross a path segment does not survive percent-encoding.

cases.architecture: MCP server on @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.17 (McpServer with registerTool/registerResource/registerPrompt) exposed both over StdioServerTransport and over a StreamableHTTPServerTransport mounted on Express 4, with every read and write going through the @aws-sdk/lib-dynamodb DynamoDBDocumentClient, and the caller's identity coming from a bearer token resolved into a DynamoDB session row over HTTP and from the invoking local process over stdio.
cases.why: Two template variables reach a readFile here as well, but neither one names a file: the attachment is found by Query on the attachments table, the caller's filename is reduced with `basename()` before it is matched against the recorded originalFilename, the path actually read is the server-written `storageKey`, and the resolved path is still required to sit under the attachment root.

cases.architecture: MCP server on @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.17 (McpServer with registerTool/registerResource/registerPrompt) exposed both over StdioServerTransport and over a StreamableHTTPServerTransport mounted on Express 4, with every read and write going through the @aws-sdk/lib-dynamodb DynamoDBDocumentClient, and the caller's identity coming from a bearer token resolved into a DynamoDB session row over HTTP and from the invoking local process over stdio.
cases.why: On the initialize request the bearer token is looked up, but an absent, unknown or expired token simply leaves `session` null and the server is built with it. A null session is the stdio contract for 'the caller is the operator who started this process': requireRole returns ok for every role and accountScope accepts a caller-supplied accountId, so an unauthenticated HTTP client gets cross-account reads plus the credit and plan-change tools. Nothing here ever answers 401.

cases.architecture: MCP server on @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.17 (McpServer with registerTool/registerResource/registerPrompt) exposed both over StdioServerTransport and over a StreamableHTTPServerTransport mounted on Express 4, with every read and write going through the @aws-sdk/lib-dynamodb DynamoDBDocumentClient, and the caller's identity coming from a bearer token resolved into a DynamoDB session row over HTTP and from the invoking local process over stdio.
cases.why: The identical `createSupportServer({ session: null })` construction, with no token handling anywhere in the file, which is correct on this transport: the process is spawned by the operator's own MCP client over a pipe, there is no remote party that could be authenticated, and it can only reach what that operator's own AWS credentials already reach.
